background: Lloyds Bank plc is the main ring-fenced bank of Lloyds Banking Group, the UK's largest retail bank, funded by UK personal and business deposits and lending mainly on residential mortgages, cards, motor finance and to UK companies.
synthesis: Rated AA- on average across all three, the weakest of them at A+ and all three on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Capital is adequate rather than strong for a UK major: CET1 of 13.6% is a shade below the median, while leverage of 5.1% is in the top quarter. Liquidity is the weaker side, with LCR of 134% and NSFR of 118% both in the bottom quarter of the group - unsurprising for a deposit-funded mortgage lender, but the least headroom of the four measures. Leverage has fallen 0.3 points since 30 Jun 2025 and the rest are broadly flat (figures to 30 Jun 2026); what has been flagged in the last 90 days is the £1.2bn Arena Television fraud litigation, a conduct exposure rather than a capital one.
